subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage: Vidya had a placement interview in three weeks, and every evening she gave herself one narrow target. Tonight it was "stop saying basically". She propped her phone on the shelf, talked for two minutes about her final-year project and played the recording back while her flatmate Naveen washed dishes. Nine "basically"s. She wrote the number on a sticky note and stuck it on the wall. Second recording, with a slow breath before each sentence: three. Naveen looked up. "That one sounded like you." Vidya circled the three, added the date, and wrote tomorrow's target under it: "finish sentences without trailing off".

qa.q: How many times did Vidya say "basically" in the first recording?
qa.a: She said "basically" nine times in the first recording.

qa.q: What might Vidya be feeling when she hears the second recording?
qa.a: She is probably relieved and encouraged, since her count fell from nine to three and it sounded like her own voice.

qa.q: Why does Vidya write the count on a note and set a new target for tomorrow?
qa.a: The written number gives honest feedback and the narrow target lets her fix one thing at a time instead of vaguely practising.

qa.q: How does Naveen's comment help Vidya?
qa.a: Naveen, who has been listening, gives an outside opinion that the second recording sounded like her, which backs up the count she measured herself.

grounding: Shows a learner setting one narrow target per session, reviewing a recording and fixing one thing at a time.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage:
"What's the target today?" Deepika asked, rolling the ball across the court.
"Elbow under the ball. Just that."
"How many shots?"
"Twenty. I'll tick each one that goes in."
"And how will you know if your elbow really was under it?"
Maria held up her phone. "You film me from the side."
They did the twenty. Afterwards they watched the clip together, pausing on shot eleven. "There. Elbow's out again when you're tired," Deepika said. Maria wrote 11 in the notebook: "elbow drifts late". "Tomorrow, same target, but ten shots, rest, ten shots." Deepika nodded. "Good. Keep it that narrow."

qa.q: How many shots did Maria plan to take?
qa.a: Maria planned to take twenty shots and tick each one that went in.

qa.q: What does Maria want to know about her elbow when she asks Deepika to film from the side?
qa.a: Maria wants honest evidence of whether her elbow really stays under the ball, because she does not trust how it feels.

qa.q: What did Maria change in her plan after watching the clip?
qa.a: She noted that her elbow drifts late and planned ten shots, a rest and ten more shots the next day with the same target.

qa.q: Why might Deepika keep the target to one thing?
qa.a: Deepika sees that fixing a single thing at once makes the feedback clear, so Maria can tell what caused any change.

grounding: Shows a learner with a narrow target per session who reviews recorded feedback and fixes one thing at a time.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage: I'm Ujjwal, and I learned public speaking in college the slow way, then the smart way. At first I just gave the same speech over and over to my mirror. Nothing changed. Then my friend Kiran, who did theatre, told me to pick one tiny thing for each session. So one evening my only goal was to stop saying "basically". I recorded a two-minute talk on my phone and played it back. I said it eleven times. Awful. Next evening, same goal. Five times. By the end of the week, zero. Then I moved on to pauses. Each session: one target, one recording, one fix. In a month I sounded like a different person.

qa.q: How many times did Ujjwal say "basically" in the first recording?
qa.a: Eleven times.

qa.q: How did Ujjwal feel hearing the first recording?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt embarrassed and dismayed, calling it awful.

qa.q: What made Ujjwal's new practice work?
qa.a: One narrow target per session, a recording to review, and fixing one thing at a time before moving on.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel hearing Ujjwal a month later?
qa.a: Kiran would likely feel pleased and proud that the advice from theatre made such a difference.

grounding: A student describes practising speaking with one narrow target per session, recording and fixing one thing at a time.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage:
Singing teacher's note, first-year music students, Week 6.
Pooja is the first student this term to use feedback properly. For her Carnatic practice she now comes with one written target, for example "hold the note in the third line of the varnam steady for four beats". She records herself on her phone, listens with me, and marks whether she met it. Last week it was the high note in the second line; she needed three sessions before it held. Her friend Nikita, by contrast, sings the whole varnam through each time and says she is "practising a lot". I've asked Pooja to show Nikita her notebook on Friday.

qa.q: How many sessions did Pooja need before the high note held?
qa.a: She needed three sessions.

qa.q: How does Pooja seem to feel about her method?
qa.a: Pooja seems calm and determined, patiently working on one target until it holds rather than rushing.

qa.q: Why does Pooja's approach work better than singing the whole piece?
qa.a: A narrow written target, a recording and a check each session give honest feedback on one fixable thing.

qa.q: How might Nikita feel when Pooja shows her the notebook?
qa.a: Nikita might feel a little defensive at first, but curious and hopeful about a way to improve faster.

grounding: A teacher's note contrasts a learner who sets one narrow target per session with recorded feedback against plain repetition.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage:
Dear Diary, Thursday.
New plan for the painting course. Vidya, the TA, said I paint every canvas top to bottom and never fix anything. True.
Today's only target: make the shadows under the apples look soft, not like black blobs. That's it. I painted three small apples, took a photo, and compared it with the reference picture. Blobs. Tried a lighter mix. Photo again. Better on the left apple. Third try, softer still.
It felt slow and a bit silly, spending two hours on shadows. But when I put today's photo next to last week's, I could actually see the difference. I feel proud. 🙂
Tomorrow: edges of the bowl. Only edges.
Anand

qa.q: What was Anand's only target today?
qa.a: To make the shadows under the apples look soft, not like black blobs.

qa.q: How did Anand feel at the end of the day?
qa.a: Anand felt proud after comparing the photos and seeing a real difference, though the session felt slow and a bit silly.

qa.q: Which parts of Anand's practice make it deliberate rather than repetition?
qa.a: A single narrow target, a photo compared with the reference after each try, and one fix at a time.

qa.q: How might Vidya react to Anand's new plan?
qa.a: Vidya would probably be pleased, since the comment about never fixing anything led to focused practice.

grounding: A student's diary shows practising with one narrow goal per session and honest feedback from photos.

Mohit: today's target: front arm high at release. only that
Pradeep: not line? not length?
Mohit: nope. one thing. recorded 12 balls on the phone propped on my kitbag
Mohit: [video]
Mohit: watched it back. arm up in 9 of 12 👍
Pradeep: nice. but look at ball 4 and ball 10
Pradeep: your landing foot goes way wide. that's why those two drifted down leg
Mohit: ugh. can't feel that from inside the action
Mohit: ok. arm stays on the list, landing foot is tomorrow's target
Pradeep: want me to film from behind? easier to see the foot
Mohit: yes pls. 6 am, nets 2
Pradeep: bring chalk, we'll draw a line for the foot
Mohit: deal 🏏

qa.q: In how many of the 12 balls was Mohit's arm up?
qa.a: In 9 of 12.

qa.q: How does Mohit feel when Pradeep points out the landing foot?
qa.a: Mohit is annoyed ("ugh") at missing it, but stays motivated and turns it straight into the next target.

qa.q: Which part of Mohit's routine makes the practice deliberate?
qa.a: Mohit picks one narrow target, records every ball, reviews the video and then chooses the next single fix, instead of just bowling more.

qa.q: How does Pradeep see Mohit's way of practising?
qa.a: Pradeep takes it seriously and wants to help, spotting the foot from the video and offering to film from behind with a chalk line.

grounding: Illustrates setting one narrow target per session, recording and reviewing the result, and fixing one thing at a time with honest feedback.
